name: Ides of March

date.source: The fed’s own result archive names the show, and its champions page dates the first Midwest Championship reign to “Mar 28th, 2003”; the results page itself is served under that date (promotions/wmw/archive/ides-of-march-2003-03-28.html).

matches.note: Squash, with a low-blow valet interference before the final Mind Cloud pin.
Matrix (c) retains, pinning off the Cyberspace. No formal ring-announcer winner line survives, only the narrated pin.
Billed “Ladysman” Noah Hanson vs “The Real Athlete” Ryan Scott. Scott wins by submission to the Legitimiser.

The title's first change. Myst runs in late with a chair; Fury superkicks the chair into Myst's face, then hits a second Fear Factor on Steele. Ring-announced: “And your winner...and new MidWest Champion...FURY!!”

A screwjob: Garvin interferes and cuffs Archangel to the ropes, Merlot beats him with a chair, and is awarded the win for being first to leave the cage once the door is cut open — confirmed only by commentary later in the show, not a ring-announcer line.

Presented as a heavily trimmed segment, no card-header convention or ring-announcer line. Sub-Beast counters an early Dess-O-Lation attempt for an uncounted pin (the referee is distracted); Dess later reverses and hits the Dess-O-Lation for the counted pin. Sub-Beast disputes the finish afterward on camera (“you stole this match”).

Main event. A screwjob: security guards (revealed afterward as a new stable, The Court) block Sub-Beast's own corner from ringside, the referee clotheslines Brad Johnson out, and Dess hits the Dess-O-Lation for the pin. Commentary only (“Dess is the new Great Lakes Champion!”), no ring-announcer line survives.

notes: All seven matches on the card are structured. Brad Johnson's opening office scene and Katy Hummer's closing reveal of The Court as a new stable are angle content, not scored bouts, and aren't separately structured; Matrix and Katy Hummer appear in both but not as match participants on this show.

name: High Stakes

date.source: The fed’s own champions page dates two title changes to 25 April 2003 and names the pay-per-view they happened on; the results page is served under that date (promotions/wmw/archive/high-stakes-2003-04-25.html). Its own newsdesk of 28 April reports the injuries from “High Stakes … at Casino Windsor”.

matches.note: Springboard cross body off an exposed-turnbuckle spot. No ring-announcer winner line survives, only the narrated pin.
Finished with Keenan's own Spiral. No ring-announcer winner line survives, only the narrated pin.

The title's first change (neither team is marked champion going in). Steele hits Ninja #1 with a chair-assisted Glacier Fall, then Scott moonsaults off the post onto Ninja #1 for the pin. Ring-announced: “Scott and Steele are the new champions!”
Rematch of the Ides of March cage match; Archangel wins clean this time with a spinebuster through a table (“To Hell and Back”).

Triple threat. Myst is champion entering (per the ring announcer); a debuting Umbrage runs in mid-match, attacks all three men, and revives the downed referee so Fury can pin Myst. Jack Gene's own call afterward is inconsistent — “Fury has retained the title” rather than “new champion” — but the champions-page ledger (see reigns.json) confirms this is the title changing back to Fury.

matches.stipulation: WMW Hardcore Championship — the High Stakes Hardcore Invitational (a 180-minute Free For All; “Mad Dog” Briskout, Mental Mikey, Hannibal, The New Breed and champion Matrix were also billed for it but don't surface at the finish — fired, dumpstered, locked in a locker, or simply absent)
matches.note: Jeff Hardkore frog-splashes Blayze through a table for the pin (“Hardkore is the Hardcore Champion!”). Not recorded as a new entry in reigns.json: the ledger's own first holder of this title's later name, the WMW Ace Superior Championship, is Jeff Hardkore from 16 May 2003 (wmw-ace-superior-r001, event=wmw-riot-2003-05-16, an uncollected show) — consistent with him already holding the plain Hardcore title out of this show three weeks earlier.

matches.stipulation: WMW Great Lakes Championship — No Disqualifications
matches.note: Main event. The Court (three interferers, none minted) and later Matrix all interfere; Matrix superkicks Sub-Beast and Dess rolls on top for the pin. No ring-announcer winner line survives, only commentary (“Dess is still the champion”).

appearances.source: Billed as an entrant in the High Stakes Hardcore Invitational; never surfaces at the show.

notes: All seven matches on the card are structured. Umbrage debuts inside match 5 (interference) and is credited there as a match participant since he re-appears at Blood Factory to challenge for the title himself; Matrix interferes in match 7 without wrestling a bout of his own on this card, credited kind:"match" for the same reason — he headlines Blood Factory a month later.

name: Blood Factory

date.source: The fed’s own champions page: the Tag Team Championship changed hands “at WMW: Blood Factory” and the new champions have held it “since May 23th, 2003”.

matches.note: A dark match ahead of the pay-per-view card itself, recapped by Benny Tyler rather than shown live (“DT is now on the main roster”). Two further dark matches are recapped the same way, without a named winner and loser resolving to registered entities — Primetime over Dragon, and the Brothers Spartan (Max named individually, partner unnamed) over Dracore and Flammin' Hot — and aren't structured here.
Benny Tyler explains in-segment that the title was just renamed from Cruiserweight to Ace Superior. Hardkore (c) retains with a downward-faith pin.
Archangel wins with a spinebuster (“from Hell and Back”).
Fury (c) retains. Ring-announced: “Here is your winner, and still WMW MidWest Champion, Fury!”

Billed “the Dream Team.” Noah Hanson submits Ryan Scott with Scott's own finisher, the Legitimizer (“He's using Ryan Scott's finisher against him! Genius!”). Ring-announced: “The Dream Team are the new tag team champions!” Post-match, Lance Steele chairs Scott's own knee in anger, and a debuting Prime Offender (billed a former UHW Champion) runs in and takes Steele out — angle content, not part of the tag match.

matches.stipulation: WMW Great Lakes Championship — Blood Factory (weapons match, four bins of ringside weapons)
matches.note: Main event. Dess (c) retains, rolling through a bridge attempt for the pin. Post-match, Matrix offers a handshake, heel-turns (“You want Cyberforce!? ...TOO BAD!!”), and The DT runs in from the crowd to hit Dess with the Destruction Driver, aligning with Matrix — an angle beat, not part of the pinfall.

notes: Six of the card's matches are structured, including a recapped-not-shown-live dark match (order 1); two further dark matches are recapped without a resolvable decision and aren't structured (see match 1's own note). Prime Offender's post-match run-in is angle content and he isn't minted from a single interference beat.
